answer: Model the agent economy as a trust graph and cap how much reputation any vertex can pass to identities it vouched into existence. Sybil clusters connect to honest agents through few edges, so a personalized random walk from trusted seeds rarely enters them; their scores stay low no matter how many fakes they mint. Fake accounts can't spiral their influence by endorsing each other, and the graph stops being a haven for cheap identities: rewards follow walk probability, not account count.
